Hangover

A handpan (hang drum) for VCV Rack, with the dirt left in · Hær · 2.0.0 · 42 HP

What it is

One whole instrument, not a voice per note. The ding sits in the middle, up to eight tone fields zigzag up both sides, and every field is always there, ringing or quiet. A strike adds energy to a field, so re-striking a ringing note builds on what is already sounding, like the real thing.

Each field rings with a fundamental, an octave and a compound fifth (the hang's tuning), plus three quieter, slightly out-of-tune shell modes that give the steel its colour. The air inside the shell is a Helmholtz resonator that speaks through the gu, the hole underneath: that is the deep "boom" when you slap the shell.

The screen shows the hang from above. Fields glow as they ring, the scale and its notes are listed, and the eight dirt bars show how much of each kind of dirt is in play. The Rattle bar flashes when something rattles.

Quick start

1. Patch L and R to your mixer (L alone gives a mono mix).
2. Send a clock divider or drum sequencer into DING, 1-8 and GU, or a poly GATE + V/OCT pair from Peal or any sequencer.
3. Pick a SCALE and KEY. Then turn DIRT from left (a clean model) to right (a battered hang in a small room).

Playing controls

ControlWhat it doesStarting point
SCALEKurd, Integral, Celtic, Amara, Hijaz, Pygmy, Equinox, Sabye, Aegean. Integral and Amara have 7 fields, so input 8 does nothing there.Kurd
KEYThe ding's note. The ding sits between G#2 and G3.D (D3)
DECAYHow long a fundamental rings, 0.4 to 12 s. Octaves and fifths die sooner, high fields sooner than low ones.about 4 s
FORCEHow hard triggers hit when VEL isn't patched.70 %
TOUCHSoft finger pad (round, dark) to hard slap (short contact, brighter, more skin and shell knock).30 %
STRIKEWhere on the field: middle = mostly fundamental, edge = more octave and fifth.30 %
MUTEA palm resting on the shell: damps everything, highest partials first. The MUTE gate does the same while high, with the sound of the palm landing.0
GULevel of the Helmholtz bass. Every strike pumps a little air; the GU trigger slaps beside the port for a full boom.50 %
ROLLSpeed of thumb rolls (6 to 24 hits a second) while the ROLL gate is high. Thumb and finger alternate on the last field played.12 /s

The dirt

Each dirt knob sets one kind of mess. The big DIRT knob scales all eight: fully left is a clean model, the middle uses the knobs as set, fully right doubles them. NEW HANG (button or right-click) rolls a new instrument: its tuning errors, beat rates, the rattling part, the loose field and the gu pitch all change. The instrument is saved with the patch.

KnobWhat's going on
TUNINGFields up to 8 cents off; their octaves and fifths up to 20-28 cents off their own fundamental, which makes a field sound sour or sweet. Hard hits start slightly sharp and settle.
BEATEach partial is really two close modes (the shell is never perfectly round), so it beats slowly, 0.3 to 4 times a second.
RATTLEA loose part on a spring (a ring, a stand, a washer) is shaken by the shell and clatters against its stops, and one loose field buzzes when it swings hard. Low settings only rattle on accents.
BLEEDThe shell knocks the neighbouring fields and the ding on every strike, and fields ring in sympathy with notes that share their partials.
AIRBreath in and out of the gu after strikes, turbulence hiss, and at high settings a faint room tone.
SKINFinger and palm noise on the steel, and now and then a fingernail.
SLOPHuman hands: late strikes (up to 12 ms), uneven force and spot, fingers that bounce back down, and grazes on a neighbouring field.
ROOMA small, warm room: early reflections and a short tail.

Jacks

JackWhat it does
DING, 1-8Triggers that strike one field each, ascending (1 = lowest tone field).
GUTrigger: a palm slap beside the port, the bass boom.
GATE, V/OCTPoly. Each rising edge strikes the field nearest that channel's pitch (0 V = C4). Unpatched V/OCT strikes the ding. Made for Peal's poly gate + pitch outs.
VELPoly 0-10 V velocity for GATE. Its first channel also sets velocity for the trigger inputs.
MUTE, ROLLGates: palm down while high; thumb roll while high.
CV rowDECAY, TOUCH, STRIKE, MUTE, GU, DIRT. Added to the knob; 10 V = the full range.
L, RStereo out, fields placed left to right as on the real shell; peaks around 5 V. L alone carries a mono mix.

Patch ideas

Groove. A drum sequencer (Ritmo, Jack or Thorax) with DING on 1 and 3, GU with the ding on the downbeat, fields 4-8 on off-beats. SLOP at 40 % makes it sound played. Patch an LFO into TOUCH so the groove breathes between pads and slaps.

Peal on a hang. Peal's poly gate and pitch into GATE and V/OCT: the bells' rows land on the nearest fields of the scale. BLEED up gives a shimmering wash between notes.

Autechre-ish. Marbles or Kleener into GATE + V/OCT, a slow random into DIRT CV, and short gate bursts into ROLL. MUTE gate from a sparse trigger chokes the hang mid-phrase.

Clean vs dirty. Right-click → "Set all dirt knobs to zero" for the clean model, then bring each dirt back one at a time to hear what it adds.

Under the hood

Every field is a set of tuned modes that are always there; nothing is a sample or a voice. What makes it behave like a real handpan:

The finger is physical. Each strike is a small mass (the fingertip) landing on a soft, lossy spring (the pad of the finger) against the moving steel. The steel pushes back, so the hit lasts as long as the physics says: a harder hit squashes the pad more and is shorter and brighter, a soft pad lingers and soaks up the top end, and striking a field that is still swinging lands differently from striking one at rest. TOUCH sets how soft and lossy the pad is.

The strike spot matters the way it does on steel. The octave and the compound fifth each have a nodal line through the middle of the field, so a dead-centre hit (STRIKE at 0) is almost a pure fundamental, and moving out brings them in. Each hit lands at a slightly different angle, more so with SLOP.

The octave blooms. The tone field is a shallow shell, so its fundamental, octave and fifth are coupled by a small nonlinearity (the 1:2:3 relation the tuner hammers in). After a hit, energy moves up from the fundamental into the octave and fifth, so the octave swells in over the first few hundred milliseconds. Hard hits bloom more; soft hits stay sweet and pure; fields whose octave is out of tune (TUNING) bloom less. The coupling only moves energy around, it never adds any, so it cannot run away.

The air is coupled to the steel. The Helmholtz resonance inside the shell is driven by every field's fundamental (the only motion that changes the volume of air inside), most of all by the ding, and the air pressure pushes back on them. Slapping beside the port (GU) still gives the full boom.

Sympathy through the shell. BLEED couples the fields with an energy-correct spring through the steel, so notes that share a partial pass it back and forth the way a real shell does, and it is stable at any setting.
